rich_summary: After their wedding, Shiva and Parvati travel to Kailasa, the radiant Silver Mountain, where gods, spirits, and nature itself celebrate their arrival. The divine couple visit Rama’s temple—where witnesses mysteriously perceive them as Rama and Sita—hinting at Shiva’s cosmic play (lila). In Kailasa, their love unfolds in intimate, joyful scenes while Nandi guards their chamber. Meanwhile the demon Taraka terrorizes the gods. Vishnu explains that only a son of Shiva can defeat him and warns the gods not to disturb the divine couple. When they finally appeal, Shiva releases his seed through yogic power, angering Parvati, who longs for motherhood and curses the gods. The seed passes through Agni, Ganga, and the mountains until it manifests as the radiant six‑headed child Skanda (Kartikeya), destined to destroy Taraka and restore cosmic balance.

top_scenes.scene_text: Shiva and Parvati arrive at glittering Mount Kailasa while gods, celestial beings, animals, and the radiant silver mountain itself seem to welcome the newlywed divine couple.
The newborn Skanda appears at dawn—six‑headed and twelve‑armed, shining like the sun—while gods shower flowers from the sky and Vedic chants resound.
The gods stand outside Shiva’s guarded chamber chanting 'Namah Sivaya' in devotion as Nandi keeps watch at the doorway of the divine couple.
